After the Trojan War, Odysseus faces a dangerous voyage back to Ithaca, meeting creatures like the Cyclops Polyphemus, Sirens, and Calypso along the way.
Written and directed by Christopher Nolan, The Odyssey is an epic fantasy adventure shot entirely with IMAX film cameras. The film stars Matt Damon as Odysseus, Tom Holland as Telemachus, Anne Hathaway as Penelope, Robert Pattinson as Antinous and Zendaya as Athena.

details.description:
Broadway Cinemas is proud to exclusively present the Paris Opera Ballet's spectacular 2026-2027 season! Kicking this season off are two world-renowned ballet classics coming straight to the big screen: Romeo and Juliet and Swan Lake.

 

Prince Siegfried is urged by his parents to choose a bride, but by the shores of a lake he meets a mysterious swan maiden, Odette, enchanted by the sorcerer Rothbart. Only a sincere vow can save her. Captivated, he swears eternal love, until he meets Odile, the black swan...

 

A magical ballet set to Tchaikovsky's sparkling music, Swan Lake was first created in 1877 for the Bolshoi Theatre in Moscow, later restaged by Marius Petipa and Lev Ivanov. Nearly a century later, Rudolf Nureyev brought his own interpretation to the Paris Opera in 1984.

details.title: A Fox Under a Pink Moon (EADF2026)
details.description:
At just 16, strong-willed Afghan sculptor and illustrator Soraya has been trying for five years to find a way out of Iran and join her mother in Austria. Married to a violent man, she is determined to shape her own future. Directed entirely remotely by Mehrdad Oskouei, this subtly textured self-portrait was filmed by Soraya over five years using her phone. Interweaving chilling escape attempts with her stunning drawings and surreal animations, Soraya pours all her worries, joys, and fears into her art.

 

Best Film Award, IDFA

details.description:
"I love my motherland, everything here." In Karabash, a polluted Russian town, beloved teacher and videographer Pavel Talankin watches his school become a state propaganda tool. Forced to promote official messages and horrified as his graduating students are recruited for war, Pavel is torn between compliance and conscience. To protect the children, he secretly documents the truth, becoming an international whistleblower. With his life at risk, he must make a dangerous escape. In an era where patriotism is weaponized, where does this "nobody" go from here?

details.description:
As economic crises deepen the gulf between politicians and the public, filmmaker Rui Pires spends a year embedded inside the Portuguese Parliament. Focusing on high-stakes debates over the Basic Housing Law, this documentary opens an unprecedented window into a political black box. Infused with irony and drama, the film captures the complex, often contradictory machinery of governance, framing the parliament as a "Palace of Citizens" to pose a sharp, uncomfortable question about the very essence of modern democracy.

 

MAX Award, Doclisboa International Film Festival
Uruguay International Film Festival

One in ten people hear voices. This documentary follows five individuals living with this phenomenon, ranging from a single protective voice to nineteen hostile ones. Within a therapeutic setting, a psychiatrist guides them in conversations directly with their internal companions. As hidden traumas surface, this revolutionary approach fosters deeper insight and acceptance. The film crafts a fascinating group portrait of these characters and their voices, reflecting the wonderful world of the human mind.

Fourteen years ago, the director survived an attempted femicide perpetrated by a classmate. In the film, she revisits those memories once more. details.description:
Like fish separated in shop jars, big city dwellers are tightly packed yet utterly isolated. In Tokyo, where 40 percent of residents face social alienation, the government even appointed a "Minister of Loneliness." As thousands seek help daily, the film follows two individuals unknowingly connected through the chat line "A Place for You," chronicling their poignant struggle for meaning. Through luminous imagery, the director tenderly captures the hopeful moment when they finally make the genuine human contact they have been missing.

details.description:
Family reunion dinner hits different when you grow up â Cringe as you rehearse the conversation in your head a thousand times before turning the knob, and putting on a show.

 

Indie legend Jim Jarmusch brings together a star-studded cast featuring Adam Driver, Cate Blanchett, Charlotte Rampling, among others, to deliver a deadpan and heartwarming family drama that clinched the Golden Lion at the Venice Film Festival. The three stories all concern the relationships between adult children, their somewhat distant parent (or parents), and each other. Each of the three chapters takes place in the present, and each in a different country. FATHER is set in the Northeast US, MOTHER in Dublin, Ireland, and SISTER BROTHER in Paris, France. Echoing the episodic structure of his early classics, the film captures the delicate dance of modern relationships, at times intimate and at times distant, shaped by tentative steps and the unexpected warmth that hits you hard and soft.

details.description:
"You come to someplace new, and everything looks just the same."
Expanding on Permanent Vacation's themes of rootless drifting, the routine of New York-based Willie is disrupted by his Hungarian cousin Eva. A year later, Willie and his friend Eddie travel to Cleveland to visit her, leading to a spontaneous road trip to Florida. Jarmusch shot the first act using leftover film stock from Wim Wenders. By piecing together mundane details to build the story, he cemented his signature minimalist aesthetic.

details.description:
Douzi, a boy with feminine features, is abandoned by his prostitute mother to an all-boys Peking opera troupe supervised by Master Guan. Douzi befriends fellow trouper Shitou.

A few years later in 1938, a teenage Douzi is trained to play dan (female roles), while Shitou learns jing (painted face male roles). When practicing the play "Dreaming of the World Outside the Nunnery", Douzi intentionally mistakes the line "I am by nature a girl, not a boy" with "I am by nature a boy, not a girl," subjecting himself to severe physical punishments. Douzi along with another student, Laizi, attempt to run away, but Douzi decides to pursue acting seriously after witnessing an opera performance. Upon returning, they find the whole troupe being punished for their desertion, and Douzi is beaten. As a result, Laizi hangs himself...
